note: On four of five criteria this is the strongest commercial fit in the batch. He is evidently successful and time-poor in the way the ICP describes — constant international travel, back-to-back meetings, summer in Mykonos, Ibiza, Saint-Tropez and Marbella — and income is not in question, since he already spends $1,500-2,000 a month on trainers and said outright that $4,000 was not the obstacle. He is emphatically not deconditioned: he lifts daily, races Hyrox for fun and ran 1:10 off a fifteen-hour flight. Good-to-great is his own framing, opened unprompted with 'I'm not here to lose 10% of body fat or anything like that. I'm just looking to change it up.' He misses only on neglected_health, and he misses it by being above it — health is the area he has least neglected, so there is no gap for the programme to close. That is the finding worth keeping: the prospect who best matches the stated ICP on success and income is the one for whom the product has least to offer, because what he needs is programming and what is for sale is accountability.
